pack.title: Dry replies & left on read
pack.description: K. Sure. Seen 9:41pm. Match the energy or end the thread with grace.

scenarios.setting: Text thread. You sent three warm paragraphs; the reply arrives in minutes.

replies.line: Got it. We can catch up later.
replies.why: It accepts a short acknowledgment without reading hostility into it.
replies.delivery: Keep the message neutral; a short reply alone does not establish their mood.

replies.why: It acknowledges the message without interpreting its brevity as hostility.
replies.delivery: Keep the message neutral; a short reply alone does not establish their mood.

replies.line: Haha — busy day? Catch me up later.
replies.why: Assuming the best gives them a graceful reason and you a graceful exit.
replies.delivery: Keep the message neutral; a short reply alone does not establish their mood.

replies.line: Message received; paragraphs taking a break.
replies.why: Self-directed humor lightens the exchange without punishing the short reply.
replies.delivery: Keep the message neutral; a short reply alone does not establish their mood.

trap.line: Wow ok. Guess I'll just stop texting you then.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

followUp.line: I wasn't sure there was more to answer; happy to catch up later.
followUp.why: It explains your pause without interpreting a short reply as rejection.
followUp.delivery: Keep the message neutral; a short reply alone does not establish their mood.

scenarios.setting: Dating app. After a good exchange, they vanish for six days, then:
scenarios.jab: hey sorry lol crazy week. wyd

replies.line: Would Thursday work for coffee? Let me know.
replies.why: It offers a concrete plan without threatening a consequence for hesitation.
replies.delivery: Offer one real time you are available; avoid a joke about the delay if you want a straightforward answer.

replies.why: No grudge, one concrete plan — their answer tells you everything.
replies.delivery: Offer one real time you are available; avoid a joke about the delay if you want a straightforward answer.

replies.line: Haha no worries — weeks happen. Still want that coffee?
replies.why: Forgiving the fade while re-offering the plan keeps it light and real.
replies.delivery: Offer one real time you are available; avoid a joke about the delay if you want a straightforward answer.

replies.line: Coffee is ready for a calendar cameo; does Thursday work?
replies.why: Humor still includes an actionable invitation.
replies.delivery: Offer one real time you are available; avoid a joke about the delay if you want a straightforward answer.

scenarios.goal: Turn an uncertain chat into a concrete invitation.

followUp.line: Send a day that works when you know; I'll leave it with you.
followUp.why: It places the next proposal with the other person without announcing an ultimatum.
followUp.delivery: Offer one real time you are available; avoid a joke about the delay if you want a straightforward answer.

scenarios.setting: Friend thread. You've been left on read for two days after asking a favor.

replies.line: Bumping this once. A no is fine too.
replies.why: It follows up once while explicitly allowing the other person to decline.
replies.delivery: Use the actual deadline and stop after one follow-up; read receipts do not reveal intent.

replies.line: Please confirm by Friday, either way.
replies.why: It gives a practical deadline and allows a refusal.
replies.delivery: Use the actual deadline and stop after one follow-up; read receipts do not reveal intent.

replies.line: No pressure either way — just need to know by Friday.
replies.why: It provides a deadline for planning while allowing either answer.
replies.delivery: Use the actual deadline and stop after one follow-up; read receipts do not reveal intent.

replies.line: My plans need a headcount by Friday; are you in?
replies.why: The light phrasing requests useful information rather than prosecuting a read receipt.
replies.delivery: Use the actual deadline and stop after one follow-up; read receipts do not reveal intent.

trap.line: Hello?? I can see you read it.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Follow up once with a practical deadline.

followUp.line: Please let me know by Friday; if you're unsure, I'll make another plan.
followUp.why: It allows an honest no while giving you a workable decision point.
followUp.delivery: Use the actual deadline and stop after one follow-up; read receipts do not reveal intent.

scenarios.setting: A friend repeatedly replies “maybe” to a plan you need to finalize.
scenarios.jab: maybe, I'll see how I feel
scenarios.goal: Set a planning deadline without demanding enthusiasm.

replies.line: Please confirm by six; otherwise I'll book for the people who are coming.
replies.why: It establishes a practical cutoff and a consequence tied to the booking.
replies.delivery: Keep the deadline practical rather than punitive, and follow through without sending repeated reminders.

replies.line: Confirm by six or I'll book without you.
replies.why: It makes the next action and deadline explicit.
replies.delivery: Keep the deadline practical rather than punitive, and follow through without sending repeated reminders.

replies.line: I'd love you to join; please let me know by six so I can finish the booking.
replies.why: It expresses welcome while explaining why a definite answer is needed.
replies.delivery: Keep the deadline practical rather than punitive, and follow through without sending repeated reminders.

replies.line: My booking form hasn't learned “maybe”; yes or no by six?
replies.why: Light humor names the planning constraint without attacking the friend's indecision.
replies.delivery: Keep the deadline practical rather than punitive, and follow through without sending repeated reminders.

followUp.jab: Why do you need to know already?
followUp.line: The reservation needs a number tonight; if you're unsure, I'll leave you out this time.
followUp.why: It connects the deadline to a real requirement and offers a workable default.
followUp.delivery: Keep the deadline practical rather than punitive, and follow through without sending repeated reminders.
